topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class and outlines the core learning objectives for the final lecture on cancer therapy.

topics.label: Localized Modalities: Surgery and Radiotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores localized intervention modalities including surgical resection and radiotherapy alongside the fundamental challenge of sparing healthy tissue.

topics.label: Cytotoxic Chemotherapy and Drug Resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the mechanisms of action, clinical applications, systemic toxicities, and efflux-mediated resistance pathways of conventional cytotoxic drugs.

topics.label: Exploiting Cancer Cell Vulnerabilities and Repair Defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain therapeutic strategies that leverage cancer-specific vulnerabilities, including hormonal dependencies, checkpoint defects, and synthetic lethality in DNA repair pathways.

topics.label: Kinase Inhibitors and Mechanisms of Resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine targeted small-molecule inhibitors of hyperactivated oncogenic kinases and the molecular adaptations driving drug resistance and addiction.

topics.label: Monoclonal Antibodies and Antibody-Drug Conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe therapeutics that use monoclonal antibodies to directly inhibit tumor signaling, initiate immune cytotoxicity, or selectively deliver cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Tumor Immunosurveillance and Checkpoint Blockade
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore host immune responses to tumors and the reactivation of exhausted T cells using immune checkpoint inhibitors targeting neoantigens.

topics.label: Adoptive and Engineered T-Cell Immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics evaluate engineered immunotherapy strategies, including bispecific engagers and CAR T cells, designed to redirect cytotoxic T cells to tumor antigens.

topics.label: Challenges, Progress, and Future Perspectives in Oncology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics reflect on historical clinical successes, contemporary therapeutic challenges, and future paradigms in cancer detection, prevention, and treatment.
